newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS-Puncak Niaga says not worried over listing.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Puncak Niaga says not worried over listing.

text.p: Malaysian water treatment firm Puncak Niaga Holdings Bhd said it was confident its shares would be well received by investors on its listing day despite the poor reception shown to recent large stock offerings.

Puncak Niaga has proven its earnings capability in the last two years, unlike the stocks of firms listed under Kuala Lumpur's infrastructure project company (IPC) category, Puncak Niaga's executive chairman Rozali Ismail said.
"Unlike the earlier IPC listings, Puncak Niaga has in fact been generating profits in the last two years...," he told Reuters in an interview.
He was responding to a question of how he expects the company's shares to perform, following recent weak investor reception to other IPC stocks.
Under Malaysia's IPC ruling, companies with a short or with no track record can seek a listing on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
Puncak Niaga expects to list its shares by the middle of next month.
The company is offering 67 million new and existing shares to the public, with the retail tranche offered at 3.80 ringgit ($1.51) each and the institutional tranche at 4.50 ringgit.

Analysts are worried over the reception shown to IPC listings, following the weak performance of YTL Power International Bhd upon its flotation last month, and the poorly-received Ekran Bhd rights issue.
At the midday close on Friday, YTL Power closed at 3.18 ringgit, well below its offer price of 3.40 ringgit.
Ekran, the main developer of the Bakun hydroelectric dam, recently completed a rights issue of 257.1 million shares which was undersubcribed by 62.77 percent.

Puncak Niaga has a concession to operate, maintain, manage and refurbish existing water treatment plants in central Selangor state and in the federal territory of Kuala Lumpur which encompasses the capital city. The 26-year concession will end on December 31, 2020.
Another concession is for the company to build new water treatment plants to be completed by 2001.

Rozali said Puncak Niaga recorded a net profit of 1.21 million ringgit from one month of operations in 1994 when it started the Selangor/Kuala Lumpur concession. It earned 40.42 million in full-year 1995 and 41.07 million last year.

"In our cash flow projection, we are expecting consistently strong and increasing cash inflows for the next 23 years based on the revenue pattern provided by the two concessions which we have secured," he said.
"The current margin of 34 percent in 1997 is expected to improve to 59 percent in 1999 and to further improve to 72 percent by the year 2002," he added.
Analysts said unlike other privatised projects, Puncak Niaga has secured better terms for its concessions.
"Compared to other IPCs, the concession agreement is more favourable for them," said Audrey Ho, head of research at Mohaiyani Securities.
"The earnings seem to be very strong," said another research chief at a Malaysian stockbroking house.
But analysts said fair valuation for the stock is just above 5.00 ringgit, which leaves little upside for short-term retail investors which dominate trading on the Malaysian bourse.

Rozali said the privatised water supply system would not necessarily lead to higher water tariffs. But he noted that the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor water systems needed major upgrading due to their age and the rapid growth.
The company is involved in developing a river project in Selangor to provide raw water at a total investment of 1.28 billion ringgit.
($1=2.52 ringgit)
